topic.title: Logarithmic Function Manipulation
topic.summary: The product, power, and change of base properties for logarithms, the natural logarithm, and how horizontal dilations of logarithmic functions become vertical translations and dilations.

lesson.title: Logarithmic Function Manipulation
lesson.summary: The product, power, and change of base properties for logarithms, the natural logarithm, and how horizontal dilations of logarithmic functions become vertical translations and dilations.
learningGoals: 2.12.A Rewrite logarithmic expressions in equivalent forms.
lesson.bigIdea: Logarithms turn multiplication into addition and powers into multiplication. Those two facts let you combine logarithmic terms into one, which is exactly what free-response Question 4 asks for.
lesson.context: Topic 2.4 rewrote exponential expressions with the properties of exponents. Each property of logarithms here is the same property read through the inverse relationship of Topic 2.10.

sections.title: 2.12.A · The product property: a horizontal dilation is a vertical translation.

blocks.text: The product property for logarithms states that log_b (xy) = log_b x + log_b y. Graphically, this property implies that every horizontal dilation of a logarithmic function, f(x) = log_b (kx), is equivalent to a vertical translation, f(x) = log_b (kx) = log_b k + log_b x = a + log_b x, where a = log_b k.
Example: log₂ (8x) = log₂ 8 + log₂ x = 3 + log₂ x. Compressing the graph of y = log₂ x horizontally by a factor of 1/8 gives the same graph as translating it up 3 units.
Combining the product property with the power property below gives a rule for quotients: log_b (x/y) = log_b (x·y⁻¹) = log_b x − log_b y. For example, log₂ 48 − log₂ 3 = log₂ 16 = 4.

sections.takeaway: log_b (xy) = log_b x + log_b y, so log_b (kx) is log_b x shifted by log_b k.

sections.title: 2.12.A · The power property: raising the input to a power is a vertical dilation.

blocks.text: The power property for logarithms states that log_b xⁿ = n log_b x. Graphically, this property implies that raising the input of a logarithmic function to a power, f(x) = log_b xᵏ, results in a vertical dilation, f(x) = log_b xᵏ = k log_b x.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: 2 ln 6 − ln 4 = ln 6² − ln 4 = ln 36 − ln 4 = ln (36/4) = ln 9. Write each step with the property it uses.

blocks.caption: Combining logarithmic terms into a single logarithm

sections.takeaway: log_b xⁿ = n log_b x: a power of the input becomes a coefficient.

sections.title: 2.12.A · Change of base: all logarithmic functions are vertical dilations of each other.
sections.conceptTitle: Change of base and the natural logarithm

blocks.text: The change of base property for logarithms states that log_b x = (log_a x)/(log_a b), where a > 0 and a ≠ 1. This implies that all logarithmic functions are vertical dilations of each other.
The function f(x) = ln x is a logarithmic function with the natural base e; that is, ln x = logₑ x.
Example: log₅ 40 = (ln 40)/(ln 5) ≈ 2.292. Also log₈ x = (log₂ x)/(log₂ 8) = (1/3) log₂ x, so the graph of y = log₈ x is a vertical dilation of y = log₂ x by a factor of 1/3.

sections.takeaway: log_b x = (log_a x)/(log_a b), and ln x = logₑ x.

vocabulary.definition: The product property for logarithms states that log_b (xy) = log_b x + log_b y.
The power property for logarithms states that log_b xⁿ = n log_b x.
The change of base property for logarithms states that log_b x = (log_a x)/(log_a b), where a > 0 and a ≠ 1. This implies that all logarithmic functions are vertical dilations of each other.
The function f(x) = ln x is a logarithmic function with the natural base e; that is, ln x = logₑ x.

connections.title: Properties of exponents, read backward
connections.body: Topic 2.4 showed bᵐbⁿ = b^(m + n). Taking log_b of both sides gives log_b (bᵐbⁿ) = m + n = log_b bᵐ + log_b bⁿ, the product property for logarithms.
connections.transferQuestion: Which property of exponents corresponds to log_b xⁿ = n log_b x?

links.label: Review the power property for exponents

connections.title: Solving equations
connections.body: Topic 2.13 uses these properties to solve exponential and logarithmic equations, and checks every solution against the domain.
connections.transferQuestion: Solve log₂ x + log₂ (x − 2) = 3 by first combining the left side.
connections.feedback: log₂ (x(x − 2)) = 3, so x² − 2x = 8 and x = 4 (x = −2 is outside the domain).
